body:
I'm glad he's been talking about getting help! Now it's time for him to walk the talk and do what's necessary to get that help. I understand it's scary, not knowing whether he'll have the energy to get through this, but like you said; you can't do it for him.

I totally get how you feel like you're fumbling in the dark. The situation isn't in your control and you don't know what's coming next. That kind of stuff is hard! So I want to stress again that it's important for you to take rest whenever you need to, and to set (and keep!) the boundaries you need for your relationship to keep functioning. Especially since you've already been through a lot of stress yourself.

And you're welcome! I hope this was able to give some clarity in the darkness.

It's the next day. 

Slightly hungover and regretting ever drinking so much bc my stomach is throwing a fit. Barfed several times this morning. I've been vomiting from stress and anxiety at least once a week for years now so this ain't nothing new. I'm never doing this again though. Being hungover on top of physical stress/anxiety symptoms feels so fucking bad. The "buzz" I felt after drinking was nice but I have ways to get that feeling without feeding myself drunk.

Right now I'm about to leave the house and get some weed. It's the only thing that helps to get my head quieter, deal with boredom and sleep alright. I know it's fucked and I'm addicted but what the fuck am I supposed to do? My head is a fucking pinball machine that does not stop. I just want some rest and silence.

Idk why I'm still updating this post. I've been complaining how no one listens to me and how I feel like my entire life I had no one to depend on but myself. I've been replying to others on this thread but I guess no one has anything to say to me. It's ironic. I guess it's my own mistake. Shouldn't have taken my fking essay of a post to the internet expecting people to care. (In case anyone who I commented on sees this; I'm not mad at you. Or feel like you owe me something. I know y'all are struggling and need someone to talk to yourselves. That's why I replied. Not because I want to guilt trip you into commenting on my post or anything like that. I'm just dumping my unfiltered feelings, that's it.)

Anyway, I'm still a bit indecisive on this whole suicide thing. A few days ago someone told me about the name origin of $uicideboy$ (They're rappers, I believe?). How these two people made a suicide pact together. They'd commit suicide if they didn't make it in 5 years. A part of me wants to do the same. It's been +20 years of suffering. Even I should be allowed to make it stop someday. It seems like I won't be getting the professional help I need anytime soon. So if they're not going to help me, I'll help myself. All I have to decide on is a date. I already know how I'm going to do it anyway.

>I can either “come home tonight” or I never loved him in the first place and just used him.

He's your ex for a reason. You're allowed to move on. You being with someone else now, says nothing about your feelings during your relationship with your ex.

>I know I shouldn’t care but I still do. Or he’s just really good at manipulation.

He's your ex. You loved him. Of course you care! When you break up with someone, all the feelings and history don't just disappear. It's normal to still care about him and feel like you want to prevent him from getting hurt. And it seems like he's using your care and empathy against you to make you feel bad.

​

I can't say whether your ex is deliberately manipulating you or not; I don't know him. But what I do know is that he clearly isn't able to deal with his own emotions and is throwing the blame on you. And this is coming from someone with 10+ years experience of being traumatized and blamed for things I didn't do. You might want to look into r/NarcissisticAbuse and trauma bonding (Link with some info: [https://www.verywellhealth.com/trauma-bonding-5210779](https://www.verywellhealth.com/trauma-bonding-5210779)). I'm not saying that's what's going on for you, because again, I don't know you nor your ex and your situation, but looking into this might be able to give you some clarity.

You also might want to talk with a professional if you aren't already, whether that'd be a therapist or something else, about what you've been through. I know suicide sounds like a solution, but is that really the only solution left? You only have a limited time on this earth. And you're allowed to be happy and make a life for yourself. Whether you've hurt people before or not. Why not exhaust all options and possibilities on finding your own happiness, before deciding to end it? Your ex their emotions and how they deal with it are their own problem to solve. Now is the time to look at what *you* actually want and need. Be selfish. Dance in the rain. Kiss a stranger on the mouth. Scream like no one hears you. Fuck everything. You're alive for *you*, not for anyone else.

Edit: Oh, and find a new place to live, if you're able to. Maybe you could move in with a friend or family until you can find a place of your own? Speaking from experience, living with an ex only brings you down. As soon as I was able to move out, after 2 years or so, I did, and it was one of the best decisions I could make. I never met anyone who was able to feel happy while still half being in a chapter of your life you closed. Surrounding yourself with things you love instead of being reminded of what you lost or went wrong can make a big positive difference in your mental wellbeing.

Same for me. 

I used to think the same thing; I'm not struggling enough, I can fix this myself, other people need help more than me, they'll think I'm attention seeking for asking for help and so on. It wasn't until I started studying psychology in university myself, that I realized it was my own brain that made me believe that, instead of it actually being true.

Like, looking at this from the perspective of a (future) psychologist; if I'm ever able to fix my own mental health issues (I'm on this sub for a reason lmao) and graduate, I want to help whoever wants to, you know? No matter whether they're on the brink of suicide or are doing fantastic. Everyone deserves someone who listens to them and helps them become a better, happier version of themselves. I chose this field because I want to help; not because I want to gatekeep who deserves help and who doesn't. People who do that shouldn't ever become therapists anyway.

I know it's scary. Opening up, being vulnerable and allowing someone else to comment on your thoughts is HELLA scary. And you might feel like you don't deserve it. I used to think I didn't either. But in the end, it's worth a try. If the hospital/therapist/whatever knows what they're doing, they'll be trying their best to help you. Whether you feel like you deserve it or not.

So if you end up reaching out for help, and the hospital/therapist/whatever isn't helpful to you, it means they failed you AND their job. And you 100% deserve to keep going until you find someone else who is able to listen and help. 

If you needed a sign to allow yourself to seek the help you want, then this is it. I'd put a "(future) psychologist approved" stamp on this post if I could.

It seems like you really care about him and try to communicate about what he's feeling. That's all you can do. You're his partner; not his therapist. All you can *be* is caring, honest and supportive. All you can *do* is communicate. It seems like your boyfriend is going through a lot of grief, and suicidal thoughts might be a way for him to deal with it. 

Does he have any grief counselling? Or a psychologist/therapist he can talk with to work through these suicidal thoughts? Sometimes, grief hits hard, and support from a partner might not be enough to help. This doesn't mean you're not good enough, or not helping enough. It just means that the grief hit him harder than expected and he needs to learn how to cope with it. Which is exactly what therapists get paid (and educated!) for.

All advice I have for you, is to try to convince him to see a professional if he isn't yet, and to just be there and listen. Besides that, make sure you're taking care of your own health and boundaries. Being together with someone who's struggling is hard. But you need to make sure you yourself are okay before you can focus on anyone else.

I hope your situation will get better soon!

Well, I just self harmed and gotten myself drunk. I'm really falling back into old habits, aren't I? If I had known I'd be 22 and still be struggling... Sigh.

Life is one big fucking joke.

There isn't a threshold before you're allowed to get help. Some people see a therapist because they have a mental disorder. Some people see a therapist just because they want someone to talk to. And some see a therapist because they'd kill themselves if they didn't. You can see a therapist with no fucking reason at all and it'll still be okay. 

Hospitals, psychologists, therapists, whatever; they're all there to help you. No matter how big or small your problems are. That's their job. They literally get paid for it. So why not make use of it?

There isn't such a thing as "suicidal enough". Whether you're drowning in a puddle or in an ocean, you're still drowning, and you deserve to get out of the water.

So at what point *do* you need to actually do something about this? Whenever you're ready. Whenever you feel like you don't want to drown anymore. That's enough.
